rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari assigns fa with adjectives three functions: ordering events in time, ranking by degree, or ordering the qualities of the things described.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري للفاء مع الصفات ثلاثة أحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa may mark causation or connection alone; it cannot coordinate a declarative statement with an imperative.
rows.anchor: النوع الثاني لمجرد السببية والربط نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa can also be a coordinating conjunction alone, as in the sequence making the vegetation dry and dark.
rows.anchor: وعكسه عكسها بمجرد العطف فيما سبق من نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In some clauses fa conveys both coordination and causation, including Moses striking the man and his death.
rows.anchor: وقد تأتي لهما نحو ﴿ فوكزه موسى فقضى عليه ﴾

words: فَٱنسَلَخَ مِنْهَا فَأَتْبَعَهُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْغَاوِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three consecutive fa particles in the account of the one who slipped away from the signs exemplify the common intermediate fa between coordinated clauses.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله تعالى ﴿ فانسلخ منها فأتبعه الشيطان فكان من الغاوين ﴾

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some grammarians distinguish a conditional answer that follows causally from one that stands in the place of an unstated consequence; these examples illustrate causality.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم إذا ترتب الجواب بالفاء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The second category is an answer that stands in place of what the first clause would cause, rather than stating a direct result.
rows.anchor: ومثال الثاني ﴿ فما يزيدهم إلا طغيانا كبيرا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa is required in a conditional answer that is not a declarative past or present verb; the source then raises cases where fa appears with such verbs.
rows.anchor: والنوع الثالث الجزائية والفاء تلزم في جواب الشرط

words: أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ
rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads the clause about one witness erring and the other reminding her with fa; the author lists it among puzzles about fa after a declarative verb.
rows.anchor: وقراءة حمزة ﴿ أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The default is that an elative indicates superiority to what it is compared with; the verse that each sign is greater than its sister seems to make each both superior and inferior.
rows.anchor: الثالثة الأصل فيه الأفضلية على ما أضيف إليه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the signs are described as great without meaningful difference; slight differences in merit can prompt differing judgments, even by one person.
rows.anchor: وأجاب الزمخشري بأن ( 4 ) الغرض وصفهن بالكبر

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Hajib says each sign is greater than its sister for observers when it occurs, since witnessing a sign affects a person more than one absent from view.
rows.anchor: وأجاب ابن الحاجب بأن المراد الأعلى أكبر من أختها عندهم وقت حصولها

rows.speaker: أحدهما
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the first blindness as blindness of the heart, which can increase or decrease, and the second as an elative meaning loss of insight.
rows.anchor: أحدهما انه من عمى القلب الذي يتولد من الضلالة وهو ما يقبل الزيادة والنقص

rows.speaker: والثاني
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes both terms literally: whoever is blind among the unbelievers here will be raised blind, so the second term is not comparative.
rows.anchor: والثاني انه من عمى العين والمعنى من كان في هذه أعمى من الكفار فإنه يحشر أعمى

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr adopts heart blindness for the first term and loss of insight for the second; he uses imala on the first but not the second, which is a noun.
rows.anchor: وإليه ذهب أبو عمرو فأمال الأول وترك الإمالة في الثاني لما كان اسما

words: ذَٰلِكُمْ أَقْسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَأَقْوَمُ لِلشَّهَٰدَةِ وَأَدْنَىٰٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When context supplies the comparison, an elative used predicatively often omits the less-preferred object of comparison.
rows.anchor: الخامسة يكثر حذف المفضول إذا دل عليه دليل وكان أفعل خبرا

rows.speaker: ابن فارس عن البصريين
rows.claim: Ibn Faris reports the Basran view that the waw means with: assemble your affairs together with your partners.
rows.anchor: فنقل ابن فارس عن البصريين أن الواو بمعنى مع أي شركائكم

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: Others understand two coordinated commands: assemble your affairs and summon your witnesses, following the wording in Noah's call.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخرون أجمعوا أمركم وادعوا شهداءكم

rows.speaker: الفارسي والفراء وجماعة من البصريين والكوفيين
rows.claim: Al-Farisi, al-Farra, and groups of Basrans and Kufans posit an omitted verb for the second conjunct when the expressed verb cannot govern it.
rows.anchor: هو قول الفارسي والفراء وجماعة من البصريين

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأصمعي واليزيدي
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda, al-Asma'i, al-Yazidi, and others treat the construction as coordination of nouns under one verb whose meaning encompasses both.
rows.anchor: وذهب أبو عبيدة والأصمعي واليزيدي وغيرهم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers ellipsis when the first verb literally applies to the next noun, but semantic inclusion when it does not; he uses examples of cutting the nose and feeding straw and water.
rows.anchor: واختار الشيخ أبو حيان 2 تفصيلا حسنا

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik says the imperative addressed to one person cannot govern the overt noun for the spouse; the sense is dwell yourself and let your spouse dwell.
rows.anchor: وجعل ابن مالك من هذا القبيل قوله تعالى

words: لَا تُضَآرَّ وَٰلِدَةٌۢ بِوَلَدِهَا وَلَا مَوْلُودٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second noun cannot be coordinated directly with the first in this construction; an omitted verb is understood: nor should a father be harmed.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى ﴿ لا تضار والدة بولدها ولا مولود ﴾

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra supplies an omitted verb, made subject to David, to coordinate the birds with the earlier object of the verse.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء التقدير وسخرنا له الطير عطفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other analyses take the birds as a comitative object, or explain the nominative reading by coordination with an implicit subject of gave.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو مفعول معه ومن رفعه فقيل على المضمر في آتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is the lasting greatest miracle and proof in every age; its reader should treat it as a major divine gift and ensure it testifies for, not against, them.
rows.anchor: بكونه أعظم المعجزات لبقائه ببقاء دعوة الاسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reader should remember the commands, prohibitions, and cautionary histories in the Quran, avoiding the disobedience that ruined those who became examples.
rows.anchor: لأن القرآن مشتمل على طلب أمور والكف عن أمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every Muslim reciting the Quran must use tartil; its minimum includes clear articulation, full pronunciation, measured breathing, reflection, and avoiding elision between letters.
rows.anchor: فحق على كل امرىء مسلم قرأ القرآن أن يرتله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view sets minimum tartil as making the recitation clear even when hurried; its fullest form pauses without stretching or dragging the reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل أقل الترتيل أن يأتي بما يبين ما يقرأ به وإن كان مستعجلا في قراءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reader should match delivery to each passage, voicing threats like someone issuing a threat and words of reverence with reverence.
rows.anchor: فإن كان يقرأ تهديدا لفظ به لفظ المتهدد وإن كان يقرأ لفظ تعظيم لفظ به على التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflect on each verse before moving on: pause at mercy to rejoice and ask for Paradise, and at punishment to heed its warning and seek refuge from the Fire.
rows.anchor: فإذا مر به آية رحمة وقف عندها وفرح بما وعده الله تعالى منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light form of لكن may be operative or non-operative: before a noun it can coordinate, while before a clause it is usually an independent corrective particle.
rows.anchor: ثم المخففه قد تكون مخففه من الثقيلة فهي عاملة وقد تكون غير عاملة فيقع بعدها المفرد

rows.speaker: صاحب البسيط
rows.claim: Al-Basit reports two analyses when a clause follows لكن: conjunction or clause-initial particle; the difference is whether pausing before it is allowed.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب البسيط اذا وقع بعدها جملة فهل هي للعطف أو حرف ابتداء قولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When waw precedes لكن, the conjunction attaches to waw and لكن serves only to mark correction.
rows.anchor: واذا دخل عليها الواو انتقل العطف اليها وتجردت للاستدراك

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisai says Arabic usage favors the light form without waw and the doubled form with waw, as in most Quranic examples.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي المختار عند العرب تشديد النون اذا اقترنت بالواو وتخفيفها اذا لم تقترن بها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra explains that the light form can coordinate without waw like bal, whereas the doubled form works like inna and is not conjunctive.
rows.anchor: وعلل الفراء ذلك بانها مخففه تكون عاطفة

rows.speaker: أكثرهم
rows.claim: Most readers lighten لكن and read rasul in the accusative, either with an omitted kana or coordinated with aba ahad; the author finds the first analysis more apt, treating لكن as clause-initial.
rows.anchor: فاكثرهم على تخفيفها ونصب رسول باضمار كان أو بالعطف على أبا أحد والأول أليق

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr doubles لكن, treats it as operative, and omits its predicate: but the Messenger of God is Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بتشديدها على انها عاملة وحذف خبرها أي ولكن رسول الله هو أي محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laalla expresses hope for a desired outcome or apprehension of an unwanted one; these states cannot literally describe God, since they imply uncertainty.
rows.anchor: لعل تجيء لمعان الاول للترجي في المحبوب

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh shifts the hope to Moses and Aaron: they are to hope Pharaoh may remember or fear, since they could not yet know that he would not believe.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating an explicit noun within one sentence is awkward and is rarely found outside poetry.
rows.anchor: وإن كان في جملة واحدة قبح الإظهار ولم يكد يوجد إلا في الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When an interrogative follows a noun to express awe or astonishment, repeating the noun is apt, though the pronoun is also possible in the example about the Fire.
rows.anchor: وإذا اقترن بالاسم الثاني حرف الاستفهام بمعنى التعظيم والتعجب كان المناسب الإظهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Names and the topic of a statement are normally explicit when first mentioned; a repeated name is usually replaced by a pronoun because the referent is already known.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الأصل في الأسماء أن تكون ظاهرة وأصل المحدث عنه كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a present tense verb functions like a noun, it takes noun-like inflection, as in the sequence of commands to seek provision, worship, and give thanks.
rows.anchor: وإذا جرى المضارع مجرى الاسم أعرب

words: وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reason to repeat an explicit noun instead of using a pronoun is to magnify or honor it; examples include repeated mention of God, the Quran's dawn recitation, and Zechariah.
rows.anchor: وللخروج على خلاف الآصل أسباب أحدها قصد التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reason is that a noun was earlier only a genitive complement, not the focus of predication, so it is made explicit when later needed as the topic.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن لأخ مذكور مضاف إليه ولم يذكر فيما تقدم مقصودا بالنسبة الإخبارية

words: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِى ٱلنَّارِ لِخَزَنَةِ جَهَنَّمَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the explicit name can cultivate awe in the hearer, like invoking the Caliph's authority; the people in Hell address the keepers of Hell by its name.
rows.anchor: السادس أن يكون القصد تربية المهابة وإدخال الروعة في ضمير السامع بذكر الاسم

words: فَإِذَا عَزَمْتَ فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُتَوَكِّلِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stating the one on whom reliance is placed strengthens the addressee's motive; repeating God's name in the next clause reinforces the appeal.
rows.anchor: السابع قصد تقوية داعية المأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explicit repetition can magnify the matter: it stresses the ease of restoring creation, the greatness of creating humanity, and the terror of the Day when mountains are shaken.
rows.anchor: الثامن تعظيم الأمر كقوله تعالى

words: إِنَّا مُهْلِكُوٓا۟ أَهْلَ هَٰذِهِ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ إِنَّ أَهْلَهَا كَانُوا۟ ظَٰلِمِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the explicit noun is more natural across two sentences than within one; it can also magnify the matter, as in the repeated word death in the cited verse and poem.
rows.anchor: قد مر أن سؤال وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر حقه أن يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Lot's people, explicit mention of the town suits the intent to destroy the settlements, which are portrayed as sharing in their people's injustice; Pharaoh's people are condemned for their qualities wherever they are.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنه لما كان المراد في المدائن لوط إهلاك القرى صرح في الموضعين بذكر القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a long stretch of intervening words, repeating the explicit noun keeps the hearer's attention from being occupied with resolving a pronoun; it is also apt at a new verse opening.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه متى طال الكلام حسن إيقاع الظاهر موضع المضمر كيلا يبقى الذهن متشاغلا

words: وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's repeated explicit name of God exemplifies the broader preference for restating a noun when the intervening material is long or a new verse begins.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى ﴿ واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intensive forms such as faʿʿāl, faʿīl, and faʿlān express more than the ordinary active participle and can count as a form of concision.
rows.anchor: تجيء اللفظة الدالة على التكثير والمبالغة بصيغ من صيغ المبالغة كفعال وفعيل وفعلان

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح
rows.claim: Abu al-Fath, from a Mu'tazili premise that human disobedience is not attributable to God, interpreted the form as meaning found rather than as causative.
rows.anchor: إن الحامل لأبي الفتح على هذا الكلام اعتقاده الاعتزالي إن معصية العبد لا تنسب إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Abu al-Fath's interpretation as weak and says a verb's intransitive or reflexive counterpart need not be joined by fa.
rows.anchor: وقد بينا ضعف كلامه وان المطاوع لايجب عطفه بالفاء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says waw rather than an expected fa leaves implicit the intervening acts: they acted on, understood, and recognized the merit of the knowledge, then praised God.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: السكاكي
rows.claim: Al-Sakkaki says the verse reports God's gift and their praise as separate actions without spelling out sequence, relying on the listener to infer their relation.
rows.anchor: وقال السكاكي يحتمل عندي أنه تعالى أخبر عما صنع بهما وعما قالا

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some infer that piety causes divine teaching from the juxtaposition of the two clauses.
rows.anchor: فظن بعض الناس أن التقوى سبب التعليم

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The investigators deny that the verse grammatically makes piety a cause of teaching: there is waw, not fa or a conditional construction, so the clauses are associated rather than causally linked.
rows.anchor: والمحققون على منع ذلك لأنه لم يربط الفعل الثاني بالأول ربط الجزاء بالشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains that whenever God gives beneficial knowledge, piety accompanies it accordingly.
rows.anchor: وحينئذ فيكون متى علم الله العلم النافع اقترن به التقوى بحسب ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired command to worship and trust illustrates coordination without a stated causal relation; after the warning against backbiting, the close calls attention to repentance from that injustice.
rows.anchor: ونظير الآية قوله تعالى ﴿ فاعبده وتوكل عليه ﴾

rows.speaker: الأئمة
rows.claim: The author notes that scholars disagree over whether the causative verb of knowing necessarily entails a corresponding mutāwaʿa form; the excerpt does not state their positions.
rows.anchor: وهاهنا بحث وهو أن الأئمة اختلفوا في أن العلم هل يستدعي مطاوعة أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise opening of al-Ikhlas reaches the utmost in declaring God's transcendence.
rows.anchor: ومن بديع الإيجاز قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse listing what the destroyed people left behind vividly warns against being deceived by a respite.
rows.anchor: وهذا بينا عجيب يوجب التحذير من الاغترار بالإمهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author includes the statement that the Day of Decision is appointed for them all among concise eloquent expressions.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ إن يوم الفصل ميقاتهم أجمعين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brief promise that the God-fearing are in a secure place is among the finest promises and warnings.
rows.anchor: وهذا من أحسن الوعد والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In three words, this command encompasses everything in the prophetic mission.
rows.anchor: فهذه ثلاث كلمات اشتملت على جميع ما في الرسالة

words: خُذِ ٱلْعَفْوَ وَأْمُرْ بِٱلْعُرْفِ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse gathers noble character: pardon joins with those who cut ties and forgives wrongdoers; enjoining right includes piety, kinship, and guarding speech; turning from fools entails patience and forbearance.
rows.anchor: فهذه جمعت مكارم الأخلاق كلها لأن في خذ العفو صلة القاطعين والصفح عن الظالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mudhāmmatān means darkened by the intensity of their greenness.
rows.anchor: قوله ﴿ مدهامتان ﴾ 3 معناه مسودتاه

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the verse's concise statement of capacity, responsibility, and earned reward as an example of eloquent concision.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two terms water and pasture encompass the earth's provisions and uses, including plants, grain, dates, fuel, clothing, fire, and salt.
rows.anchor: فدل بأمرين على ججميع ما أخرجه من الأرض

words: يُسْقَىٰ بِمَآءٍ وَٰحِدٍ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَهَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فِى ٱلْأُكُلِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Different tastes and scents despite shared water and soil attest to God's subtle power and unity; otherwise plants of the same kind in one place would not differ.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو كان ظهور الثمرة بالماء والتربة لوجب في القياس ألا تختلف الطعوم والروائح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two denials remove all defects of wine; the second also encompasses loss of reason, money, and drink.
rows.anchor: كيف نفى بهذين جميع عيوب الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast shows the value of hearing and sight: deafness is paired with lack of intellect, while blindness is paired only with loss of sight.
rows.anchor: فدل على فضل السمع والبصر حيث جعل مع الصم فقدان العقل ولم يجعل مع العمي إلا فقدان البصر

words: لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb akhadha has several senses, including usurpation, as in the report about taking even a handspan of land.
rows.anchor: تجىء بمعنى غصب ومنه من أخذ قيد شبر من أرض طوق من سبع أرضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhadha and its derivatives can mean punish or seize in retribution, as in the cited accounts of God taking unjust peoples and the prayer not to be called to account.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى عاقب كقوله تعالى ﴿ وكذلك أخذ ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction akhadha yafʿalu can mean beginning to do something, like jaʿala yafʿalu and karuba yafʿalu.
rows.anchor: وتجىء للمقاربة قالوا أخذ يفعل كذا كما قالوا جعل يقول وكرب يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhadha may introduce an oath or solemn covenant, as in God's taking a pledge from the People of the Book and the covenant taken from the Israelites.
rows.anchor: وتجىء قبل القسم كقوله تعالى ﴿ وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the command to take what was given firmly, akhadha means act upon the command and avoid the prohibition with diligence.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى اعمل كقوله تعالى ﴿ خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative particle la can negate the speaker's or addressee's present or future action; it can also enter past-tense oath or prayer formulas and ordinary past clauses.
rows.anchor: والنفي بها يتناول فعل المتكلم نحو لا أخرج اليوم ولا أسافر غدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La is usually repeated in a coordinated negative, but may appear once, as in the statement that he neither believed nor prayed.
rows.anchor: والأكثر تكرارها وقد جاءت غير مكررة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فلا اقتحم العقبة ﴾

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the single la is repeated in meaning: the man did not free a slave or feed a needy person; another view treats it as an imprecation that he should do good.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري لكنها مكررة في المعنى لأن المعنى لا فك رقبة ولا أطعم مسكينا

words: رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some call prohibitive la a request particle so the label includes supplication as well as prohibition; here la is a prayer asking God not to hold the speakers accountable.
rows.anchor: وترد للدعاء نحو ﴿ لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ﴾ 5 ولذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some constructions with la can be read either as negation or prohibition.
rows.anchor: وقد تحتمل النفي والنهي كقوله تعالى ﴿ ألا تعبدوا إلا الله ﴾ 6 ﴿ وما لكم لا تقاتلون ﴾ 7

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a response particle, la contradicts yes or bala; after a confirming question the answer is bala, while a genuine question takes la or naʿam.
rows.anchor: الثالثة إن تكون جوابية اي رد في الجواب مناقض
